case.case_title: Gnanamuttu v. Military Officer Ananda and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1999] 2 Sri LR 213

clause.text: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner’s detention and arrest without possession of a Police Registration Form violated his right to equality and equal protection under Article 12(1) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner argued that his arrest and detention were arbitrary, unlawful, and violated his fundamental rights under Article 12(1) as he was treated differently from other passengers despite producing valid identity documents.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents contended that the petitioner was detained due to suspicion of terrorist activities and that the arrest was lawful. They also argued the Magistrate acted properly based on the B Report presented.
key_facts: Petitioner was stopped at an Army checkpoint and asked for a Police Registration Form which he did not possess.
Petitioner produced National Identity Card, Driving Licence, and Student Identity Card as proof of identity.
Petitioner was detained while other passengers were released.
Petitioner was taken to Police Station, finger-printed, and produced before Magistrate on a B Report alleging suspicion of terrorist activities.
Petitioner was discharged by the Magistrate on 20.02.1998.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 12(1) guarantees equality before the law and equal protection, meaning no person should be arbitrarily detained or treated differently without lawful basis. Possession of a Police Registration Form was not a legal requirement justifying detention.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found the petitioner’s identity was sufficiently established by the documents he produced, and there was no legal basis for his detention or arrest solely for not possessing a Police Registration Form. The detention was discriminatory and violated Article 12(1).
principles_established: Detention without lawful basis violates the right to equality before the law.
Possession of a Police Registration Form is not a legal requirement for identity verification.
Police and Magistrate must act within constitutional limits respecting fundamental rights.

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s fundamental rights under Article 12(1) were infringed by his unlawful detention and arrest. The petitioner was entitled to compensation.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The petitioner was awarded Rs. 50,000 as compensation, with Rs. 42,500 payable by the State and Rs. 7,500 personally by the 2nd respondent, payable within three months.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(1) was central to the court’s reasoning as it protects individuals from arbitrary detention and ensures equal treatment before the law, which was violated in this case by detaining the petitioner without lawful justification.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The documents produced by the petitioner were more than sufficient to ascertain his identity. There was no basis for the 1st respondent to have detained the petitioner, and no basis for the 2nd respondent to have produced him before the Magistrate's Court on a “B“ Report. The petitioner's rights under Articles 12 (1) and 13 (1) of the Constitution were infringed by such action.
